Thirty years I've been working this land. My mother farmed before me, and her mother before that. In Quzhou, everyone does wheat then maize — that's just how the year goes. My land is flat and the soil is decent. I have a well, so water is not my worry, though pumping costs money.

I only have 4.1 mu and two mouths to feed, plus I need to sell some grain. I have to be careful with spending because my husband and I live on what this land gives us.

**For winter wheat:** I'll plant all 4.1 mu after maize harvest in October. I go to the village supply store and buy whatever improved wheat seeds they are selling this year — I don't save my own seed anymore, the shop seed gives better yield. I'll rotary-till the field first, mix in compound fertilizer, then sow. In spring I'll spread urea when the wheat starts jointing. For water, I always do four times: before sowing to settle the seed, one winter watering to protect against freeze, jointing, and then again at heading. I spray herbicide in winter while plants are small, and I watch for aphids and rust before summer — usually one more spray.

**For summer maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June I plant maize. No time to waste, we have to move fast. I always buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the store has. I do direct seeding without plowing, just open furrows. Summer rains help a lot so I only pump water twice: once at sowing if it's dry, and once during silking if there's no rain. I put fertilizer down at planting and add urea when the plants are knee-high. I watch for corn borer and spray once if I see it bad.
